rules.statement: Use an approved governed component or pattern whenever one exists for the required UI responsibility.
rules.rationale: Reimplementing governed behavior with custom markup or CSS bypasses the component contract, semantics, states, RTL behavior, and package boundary.

rules.statement: Do not invent component props, variants, states, events, slots, or behaviors that are not declared by the approved contract.
rules.rationale: The public contract is the component API authority. Figma-only axes and Storybook fixture behavior do not create runtime API.

rules.statement: Use an existing governed token when it already owns the visual or layout decision.
rules.rationale: Using the token preserves system intent, mode behavior, future updates, and machine-verifiable connectivity.

rules.statement: Do not author raw product UI colors when a semantic design-system color token is required.
rules.rationale: Raw product colors bypass Light/Dark semantics and make generated UI diverge from the governed system.

rules.statement: Author local CSS only for product or composition decisions that are explicitly outside component ownership and have an approved authority.
rules.rationale: Custom CSS is sometimes necessary for product composition, but it must not become a hidden substitute for missing component or pattern governance.

rules.statement: A local raw dimension must be supported by explicit product/Figma evidence or approved composition guidance when no governed token owns the value.
rules.rationale: A visually plausible number is not sufficient authority for an AI-generated layout.

rules.statement: Do not infer product composition rules from Storybook fixture layout or finished prototype source.
rules.rationale: Storybook includes evidence-frame dimensions and answer implementations that are intentionally not product authoring authority.

rules.statement: When the same non-trivial composition decision recurs across product surfaces, treat it as a candidate for approved composition guidance or a governed pattern instead of repeatedly inventing local CSS.
rules.rationale: Repeated human judgment is evidence that the design system may be missing reusable machine-readable knowledge.

rules.statement: Use logical layout properties and inherit the surrounding writing direction unless a narrower content direction is explicitly justified.
rules.rationale: Logical layout preserves RTL/LTR behavior without duplicating physical left/right implementations.

rules.statement: Set a narrower LTR or RTL direction only for content whose intrinsic direction is known from product semantics, such as an email address or project key.
rules.rationale: Mixed-direction product data sometimes needs isolation, but arbitrary direction overrides break shell and component mirroring.

rules.statement: Mirror an icon in RTL only when approved asset or usage guidance identifies the icon as directional.
rules.rationale: Navigation arrows and chevrons may mirror, while semantic symbols such as close, search, and status icons generally must not be guessed as directional.

rules.statement: Preserve the native and ARIA semantics, focus ownership, keyboard behavior, and accessible naming required by component and pattern contracts.
rules.rationale: Visual similarity does not make a generated composition valid if it changes the governed interaction or accessibility model.

rules.statement: Treat Storybook as a human-visible evidence and evaluation surface, not as the source of truth for AI authoring decisions.
rules.rationale: Canonical authoring rules must remain machine-readable and independently consumable by an agent.

rules.statement: During an isolated evaluation or demo, a deterministic placeholder value may be used only when the production generation or allocation rule is unresolved, the placeholder is explicitly labeled as non-production evidence, and it does not assert a production format, allocation rule, or reusable product behavior.
rules.rationale: Evaluation evidence sometimes needs an inspectable value even when production generation is unresolved; explicit non-production labeling preserves the unresolved system decision instead of hiding it behind a guessed product rule.

rules.statement: When contracts, tokens, approved composition guidance, and supplied product evidence do not authorize a required decision, mark the decision unresolved instead of inventing a rule.
rules.rationale: An explicit gap is useful design-system evidence; an invented answer hides the gap and prevents reliable AI-readiness evaluation.

forbidden: raw product colors that bypass semantic color tokens
custom reimplementation of a governed component or pattern responsibility
invented component variants, states, props, events, or slots
copying Storybook fixture dimensions into product UI without independent authority
escalateWhen: no approved authority exists for a required styling decision
a non-trivial composition rule repeats across product surfaces
the requested UI requires behavior explicitly forbidden by the nearest governed component contract

may: render canonical AI authoring rules for human review
visualize approved composition guidance after that guidance exists
host blind AI-generated outputs after generation for evaluation
use clearly labeled local evidence-frame dimensions for deterministic documentation and test canvases without granting those values product-authoring authority
mustNot: be the only source of an AI authoring rule
be supplied as answer implementation source during a blind generation task
turn evidence-frame dimensions into product authoring guidance
